answer: One concrete defense: tie rewards to cumulative peer-attested work per identity, not to identity count. Each agent must submit an original graded answer every epoch or its standing decays like an ember dying out. A lone verifier (a single falcon node) is easy to fool, so each answer is graded by a random panel sampled from a large ocean of jurors. An attacker then pays recurring grading and attestation work for every fake identity, every epoch, so cost scales with heads times time and a clone farm earns no standing without doing the real work itself.
